state.case_summary:
A woman in her 50s was brought to the emergency department after she collapsed, received chest compressions from her husband, and recovered consciousness at home. On admission, the patient was conscious without any discomfort.

Vital signs were normal and physical examination was unremarkable.

- ECG Findings:    - 12-lead ECG showed sinus rhythm with normal QRS and QT intervals, normal TU waves, no J-point or ST-segment elevation, and no conduction abnormalities. Remarkable for repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes with atypical left bundle-branch block/left axis deviation–like morphology and short-coupling interval of 240 milliseconds.    - Continuous ECG monitoring revealed recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, some deteriorating into ventricular fibrillation.      - Laboratory Tests:    - Serum electrolyte levels were normal      - Imaging Studies:    - Transthoracic echocardiography showed normal cardiac function and structure    - Emergency coronary angiography showed no evidence of obstructive coronary artery disease      - Genetic Testing:    - Revealed a variant of unknown significance in the coding gene of cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2)      - Figures:    Figure A Title: 12-lead ECG    Description: Shows repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes with atypical left bundle-branch block morphology        Figure B Title: Rhythm Strip    Description: Shows sinus rhythm with frequent premature ventricular depolarizations, one inducing polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
